title: „Post-Resuscitation Interdisciplinary MUlticenter Study”
summary:
After cardiac arrest, people may experience lasting difficulties despite successful resuscitation. These can include reduced physical abilities, problems with memory and concentration, and psychological distress. Family members may also be affected by the event and the care that follows.

The study at University Medical Center Mannheim and Klinikum Stuttgart investigates factors associated with recovery and long-term difficulties. It establishes a shared research resource for several related projects. These projects examine changes in the body's immune defences, blood measurements that may help predict recovery, and whether the breakdown of red blood cells affects the reliability of these measurements. The central question is whether certain blood measurements of immune function during the first days after resuscitation are associated with difficulties six months after hospital discharge.

Up to 700 adult patients will be enrolled and followed over time. In addition to information from usual medical care, extra blood volumes will be collected during blood sampling that would take place anyway. Samples will be obtained on days 0, 1, 3 and 5 after circulation has been restored and three, six and twelve months after hospital discharge. Follow-up visits will assess physical abilities, memory, psychological well-being and quality of life using standardized tests and questionnaires.

Existing medical records from previously treated patients will also be analysed for selected comparisons. Approximately 100 family members and close persons may participate in questionnaires about their burden and quality of life after giving their own consent. Medical treatment is not determined by the study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient cohort:
- Non-traumatic out-of-hospital and/or in-hospital cardiac arrest treated with cardiopulmonary resuscitation and resulting in return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC).
- Intensive care treatment at University Medical Center Mannheim or Klinikum Stuttgart.
- German language proficiency in accordance with the study protocol requirements for informed consent and questionnaire assessments.
- Both patients with and without capacity to provide informed consent are eligible. For patients lacking capacity, consent is obtained from a legally authorized representative; personal informed consent is obtained when capacity is regained.

Family member cohort:
- Family members or close persons of enrolled patients.
- Personal informed consent to participate in the PICS-F questionnaire assessments.
Exclusion criteria:
The following exclusion criteria apply to the patient cohort:
- Age below 18 years.
- Pregnancy.
- Traumatic out-of-hospital or in-hospital cardiac arrest.
- Refusal to participate in the study.
- Risk to study personnel arising from blood sampling, for example due to highly contagious infectious diseases.
- Non-German-speaking patients, in accordance with the language restriction specified in the study protocol.

The patient-specific exclusion criteria do not automatically apply to the family member cohort. Family members and close persons participate only after providing their own informed consent.
